cues.en: Hello, this is Tony Heller from realclimatescience.com,
cues.zh: 大家好，我是 realclimatescience.com 的 Tony Heller，

cues.en: the climate guy setting the record straight about climate.
cues.zh: 一位为气候问题澄清事实的气候专家。

cues.en: This video is titled A Century of US Cooling Erased by NOAA.
cues.zh: 这段视频的标题是《NOAA 抹去了美国一个世纪的降温记录》。

cues.en: The United States has by far the most complete and accurate temperature record in the world, known as the United States Historical Climatology
cues.zh: 美国拥有全球最完整、最准确的气温记录，这套记录被称为美国历史气候

cues.en: Network.
cues.zh: 网络。

cues.en: It consists of about 1,200 thermometers
cues.zh: 它由大约 1,200 支温度计组成，

cues.en: relatively evenly spaced across The United States.
cues.zh: 这些温度计相对均匀地分布在美国各地。

cues.en: Every month, NOAA, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration,
cues.zh: 每个月，美国国家海洋和大气管理局（NOAA）

cues.en: publishes graphs like this one.
cues.zh: 都会发布类似这样的图表。

cues.en: The graph is based almost entirely on data from the United States Historical Climatology Network and purports to show about 1.5 degrees warming since 1910.
cues.zh: 这张图表几乎完全基于美国历史气候网络的数据，声称自 1910 年以来气温上升了约 1.5 度。

cues.en: There's a huge problem though. This graph is not an accurate representation
cues.zh: 但这里有个巨大的问题。这张图表并没有准确反映

cues.en: of the thermometer data.
cues.zh: 温度计测得的实际数据。

cues.en: The actual measured thermometer data from the United States Historical Climatology Network, the blue line here, shows that The US has actually been cooling over the last century.
cues.zh: 来自美国历史气候网络的实际温度计测量数据（即此处的蓝线）显示，美国在过去一个世纪里其实一直在降温。

cues.en: But before NOAA releases their graphs to the public, they massively manipulate the data to turn this cooling trend into a warming trend. The red line shows the graphs which they released to the public.
cues.zh: 但NOAA在向公众发布图表之前，大幅篡改了数据，把这一降温趋势变成了升温趋势。红线表示他们向公众发布的图表。

cues.en: This next graph shows the hockey stick of adjustments which NOAA makes to The US temperature record.
cues.zh: 下一张图展示了NOAA对美国温度记录所做调整的“曲棍球棒”。

cues.en: In the years before 2000,
cues.zh: 在2000年之前的那些年里，

cues.en: they increasingly subtract from the actual measured temperature.
cues.zh: 他们越来越多地从实际测量的温度中减去数值。

cues.en: In 1920, it was about one degree of subtraction.
cues.zh: 1920年，大约减去了1度。

cues.en: And in the years after 2000, they add to the measured temperature, about half a degree last year. So remember, they subtracted about one degree in 1920 and they add about half a degree now. That accounts for the entire 1.5
cues.zh: 而在 2000 年之后，他们把测得的温度调高了，去年大约调高了半度。所以记住，他们在 1920 年左右调低了约一度，现在又调高了约半度。这就解释了他们图表中显示的全部 1.5

cues.en: degrees warming they show in their graph.
cues.zh: 度升温。

cues.en: So the implication is that the entire 1.5
cues.zh: 所以这意味着，NOAA 向公众公布的整个 1.5

cues.en: degree warming trend, which NOAA releases to the public, is due to manipulation by NOAA scientists.
cues.zh: 度升温趋势，都是 NOAA 科学家操纵数据造成的。

cues.en: So US warming is not due to carbon dioxide,
cues.zh: 所以美国的气温上升并不是因为二氧化碳，

cues.en: it's actually due to data tampering.
cues.zh: 实际上是因为数据篡改。

cues.en: This is the actual measured trend The US has been cooling for a century.
cues.zh: 这才是实际测得的趋势，美国过去一个世纪一直在降温。

cues.en: Now let's look at their data manipulations using a different metric along the x axis. This time we're going to use atmospheric
cues.zh: 现在我们换个横轴指标，来看看他们的数据篡改手段。这次我们要用大气中的

cues.en: CO2.
cues.zh: 二氧化碳浓度。

cues.en: When atmospheric CO2 was about 300 parts per million a century ago, they subtracted one degree from the measured temperature.
cues.zh: 一个世纪前，当大气中的二氧化碳浓度约为 300 ppm 时，他们从实测温度中减去了 1 度。

cues.en: And now that CO2 is 400 parts per million, they're adding about half a degree onto the measured temperature.
cues.zh: 如今二氧化碳浓度已达400ppm，他们就在实测温度上加了约半度。

cues.en: But the interesting thing about this graph is that it makes a very straight line. Their data tampering correlates almost perfectly with atmospheric CO2
cues.zh: 但这张图有意思的地方在于，它画出了一条非常直的线。他们的数据篡改几乎与大气二氧化碳完美相关，

cues.en: with an r squared of 0.98.
cues.zh: R方高达0.98。

cues.en: So what they're doing is they're precisely tampering with the data to match their own global warming theory.
cues.zh: 所以他们干的事，就是精确地篡改数据，去迎合他们自己的全球变暖理论。

cues.en: Junk science doesn't get any worse than this.
cues.zh: 伪科学恶劣到这个地步，也算是登峰造极了。

cues.en: Now going back to their adjustment versus time graph, we can see that there's a very sharp spike after the year 1970.
cues.zh: 现在回到它们的调整幅度随时间变化的图表，可以看到 1970 年后出现了一个非常尖锐的峰值。

cues.en: Let's look at how they did that.
cues.zh: 来看看他们是怎么做到的。

cues.en: Every month, a certain number of stations doesn't report the temperature. When they don't report, NOAA simply fabricates
cues.zh: 每个月都有一定数量的气象站没有上报温度。遇到这种情况，美国国家海洋和大气管理局会直接编造

cues.en: a temperature for that station using a computer model.
cues.zh: 该站的温度数据，并用计算机模型来生成。

cues.en: This graph shows the percent of fabricated data since the year 1960.
cues.zh: 这张图显示了自 1960 年以来编造数据的比例。

cues.en: Until about the year 1980,
cues.zh: 直到大约 1980 年，

cues.en: about 10% of The United States historical climatology network data was fabricated. But since then, it's been greatly increasing.
cues.zh: 美国历史气候网络的数据中约有 10% 是编造的。但从那以后，这一比例大幅上升。

cues.en: Now they're fabricating over 40%
cues.zh: 现在他们伪造的数据超过了 40%。

cues.en: of the data.
cues.zh: 的数据。

cues.en: By fabricating data, they can create any shaped graph they want.
cues.zh: 通过捏造数据，他们想要什么样走势的图表，就能画出什么样的图表。

cues.en: And looking at their adjustments versus time graph again, we can see that right when they started fabricating a lot of data, that was when the real blade of their hockey stick occurred.
cues.zh: 再来看一下他们调整幅度随时间变化的图表，我们能发现，正是在他们开始大量伪造数据的时候，“曲棍球棒”的真正冰刃部分出现了。

cues.en: So their big warming spikes since 1980 shown here is due largely to fake data. It's not even coming from thermometers.
cues.zh: 所以这里显示的自 1980 年以来的急剧升温，很大程度上都是由于虚假数据导致的，甚至都不是来自温度计的实测数据。

cues.en: Now let's look at the history of their data tampering. This is a story of the New York Times from 1989.
cues.zh: 现在来看看他们篡改数据的历史。这是1989年《纽约时报》的一篇报道。

cues.en: US data since 1895
cues.zh: 美国自1895年以来的数据

cues.en: failed to show warming trend, 01/26/1989.
cues.zh: 未能显示变暖趋势，1989年1月26日。

cues.en: Washington, January 25.
cues.zh: 华盛顿，1月25日。

cues.en: After examining climate data extending back nearly one hundred years, a team of government scientists has concluded there's been no significant change in average temperatures or rainfall in The United States over that entire period.
cues.zh: 在考察了近一百年前至今的气候数据后，一组政府科学家得出结论：在整个这段时期内，美国的平均气温或降雨量都没有显著变化。

cues.en: The study made by scientists for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration,
cues.zh: 由美国国家海洋和大气管理局的科学家开展的这项研究，

cues.en: NOAA, was published in the current issue of geophysical
cues.zh: 美国国家海洋和大气管理局（NOAA）的这项研究，发表在最新一期的《地球物理研究快报》上。

cues.en: research letters.
cues.zh: 《地球物理研究快报》。

cues.en: So in 1989,
cues.zh: 所以在1989年，

cues.en: no one knew that The United States climate was not changing.
cues.zh: 没人知道美国的气候并没有变化。

cues.en: And another report made by NASA in 1999,
cues.zh: NASA在1999年发布的另一份报告，

cues.en: authored by NASA's top climate alarmist James Hansen, said The United States was actually cooling.
cues.zh: 由NASA最著名的气候警报主义者James Hansen撰写，报告称美国实际上正在变冷。

cues.en: Wither US climate by James Hansen and others, August 1999.
cues.zh: 《美国气候将走向何方》，James Hansen等人，1999年8月。

cues.en: Empirical evidence does not lend much support to the notion that climate is headed precipitately towards more extreme heat and drought. The drought of nineteen ninety nine covered a smaller area than the nineteen eighty eight drought when the Mississippi almost dried up. And the nineteen eighty eight drought was a temporary inconvenience as compared with repeated droughts during the nineteen thirties Dust Bowl that caused an exodus from the Prairies as chronicled in Steinbeck's Grapes of Wrath.
cues.zh: 经验证据并不太支持这种观点，即气候正急剧走向更极端的酷热与干旱。1999 年的干旱受灾面积小于 1988 年那次，当时密西西比河几乎干涸。而与 1930 年代“沙尘暴”期间的连年大旱相比，1988 年的干旱只算是一场暂时的小麻烦，那场大旱导致了大草原地区的人口大迁徙，就如 Steinbeck 在《愤怒的葡萄》中所记录的那样。

cues.en: In The US, there has been little temperature change in the last fifty years, the time of rapidly increasing greenhouse gases.
cues.zh: 在美国，过去五十年温度变化很小，而这正是温室气体快速增加的时期。

cues.en: In fact, there was a slight cooling throughout much of the country. Figure two.
cues.zh: 事实上，全国大部分地区还略有降温。见图二。

cues.en: And this was the NASA 1999
cues.zh: 这是NASA 1999年的

cues.en: graph. It showed that 1934
cues.zh: 图表。它显示1934年

cues.en: was the warmest year in The United States and that temperatures had declined since the nineteen thirties.
cues.zh: 是美国最暖的一年，而且自上世纪三十年代以来气温已经下降。

cues.en: Now I'm going to flash back and forth between NASA's 1999
cues.zh: 现在我要在NASA 1999年的

cues.en: graph and their 2015 graph.
cues.zh: 图表和他们2015年的图表之间来回切换。

cues.en: to turn what was formerly a cooling trend into a warming trend.
cues.zh: 从而把原本的降温趋势变成了升温趋势。

cues.en: The warming shown in The US temperature record is due to data tampering,
cues.zh: 美国温度记录中显示的升温，是数据被篡改造成的，

cues.en: not due to what's been read from the thermometers.
cues.zh: 并非温度计读数所显示的结果。

cues.en: And the NASA temperature data is based largely on the manipulated temperature data from NOAA.
cues.zh: NASA 的温度数据很大程度上基于 NOAA 篡改过的温度数据。

cues.en: So after 1999,
cues.zh: 所以，1999 年之后，

cues.en: the decision was made to get rid of The US cooling and turn it into warming.
cues.zh: 他们决定抹去美国的降温趋势，把它变成升温趋势。

cues.en: So now let's look at why The US temperature data is so important.
cues.zh: 现在我们来看看为什么美国的气温数据如此重要。

cues.en: In 1880, the majority of the NOAA daily temperature database is located in The United States.
cues.zh: 在 1880 年，NOAA 日气温数据库的大部分数据都来自美国。

cues.en: They had no temperatures from Russia,
cues.zh: 他们当时没有来自俄罗斯的气温数据，

cues.en: Asia, very little in Africa, none in South America,
cues.zh: 亚洲也没有，非洲极少，南美洲完全没有，

cues.en: and very little in Australia.
cues.zh: 澳大利亚也少得可怜。

cues.en: the situation wasn't much better. Once again, the majority of the NOAA daily temperature database was located in The United States.
cues.zh: 情况并没有好转多少。NOAA 日气温数据库的大部分数据依然来自美国。

cues.en: None in South America, very few in Africa, very few in Asia. They started to get a few in Russia.
cues.zh: 南美洲没有，非洲极少，亚洲极少。俄罗斯开始有几个了。

cues.en: the situation had improved somewhat, but once again, the global temperature record was still dominated by The United States. They only had one station in South America,
cues.zh: 情况有所改善，但全球温度记录仍由美国主导。南美洲只有一个站点，

cues.en: it's once scattered around wide ranging area of Siberia and Russia. So that's why this data tampering in The United States is so important. The United States is the only large area in the world with a coherent long term daily temperature database.
cues.zh: 零星散布在西伯利亚和俄罗斯的广阔区域。所以这就是为什么美国的数据篡改如此重要。美国是世界上唯一拥有连贯长期每日温度数据库的大区域。

cues.en: By tampering with The US temperature record, NOAA is by default tampering with the global temperature record on a very large scale.
cues.zh: 通过篡改美国的温度记录，NOAA 实际上也在大范围篡改全球温度记录。

cues.en: The work of climate scientists around the world depends on the accuracy of NOAA NASA temperature data. And if that data has been skewed, then the results of this climate scientist research is also going to be skewed.
cues.zh: 世界各地气候科学家的研究都依赖 NOAA 和 NASA 温度数据的准确性。如果这些数据被扭曲了，那么气候科学家的研究结果也会被扭曲。

cues.en: I released the software I used to generate this graph to the public years ago, and so far nobody's found anything wrong with it. This data tampering is very real.
cues.zh: 几年前，我就公开了生成这张图表所用的软件，至今没人发现任何问题。数据篡改确实存在。

cues.en: US government scientists are precisely tampering with the temperature data to match their global warming theory.
cues.zh: 美国政府的科学家们正是通过篡改气温数据，来迎合他们的全球变暖理论。

cues.en: What I've shown you here today is incredibly bad science, but it's standard operating procedure in climate science.
cues.zh: 我今天在这里向大家展示的，是极其糟糕的科学研究，但这却是气候科学领域的标准操作。
